rubric.label: Insight Expression
rubric.reason: The visualization effectively addresses all five insight goals in a well-structured 2x2 panel layout. Panel A aligns NASDAQ trajectories with rebased indices and marks both peaks (dot-com peak at 305 in March 2000, AI-era high at 149 in Q4 2024), directly serving the bubble-era-parallel and peak-markers goals. Panel B clearly shows P/E ratio divergence with annotated values (105.2× vs 40.3×) and a highlighted shaded region emphasizing the magnitude difference. Panel C contrasts IPO volumes side-by-side with clear value labels showing the dramatic difference (308 vs 37 in comparable years), fulfilling the ipo-frenzy-contrast goal. Panel D shows earnings as a backdrop with dual y-axes and an annotation about AI-era earnings being ~17× dot-com levels, supporting the earnings-backdrop goal. The title poses a compelling narrative question. Minor issues: the earnings panel annotation text is somewhat cramped and partially overlapping, the dual y-axes in Panel D require careful reading, and some label overlaps exist (e.g., Panel A title overlaps with the peak annotation). These are relatively minor and don't fundamentally obstruct the insights. The overall story is clear: the AI era shows a much more moderate trajectory in price, P/E, and IPO activity, with far stronger earnings support.

(2) pe-ratio-divergence: Panel B clearly shows dot-com P/E peaking at 105.2× vs AI-era 40.3×, with an annotation noting '2.6× the AI-era peak.' (3) ipo-frenzy-contrast: Panel C contrasts IPO volumes year-by-year across eras, showing the dot-com surge (308 in 1999) vs much lower AI-era numbers. (4) earnings-backdrop: Panel D shows aggregate NASDAQ-100 earnings for both periods with dual axes and an annotation noting AI-era earnings are ~17× dot-com levels, contextualizing valuations. (5) peak-markers: Panel A marks the dot-com peak (305, Mar 2000) and AI-era high (149, Q4 2024) on the aligned timeline. The editorial tone, analytical density, and narrative-driven style targeting analysts are all well executed.
